purpose: Record the bounded repository-provider and workflow-authority invariants changed by the FCR split merge membrane, pull-request-only GitHub App authority, and exact-head Quality Gate repair; this is review evidence, not a live provider or production claim.

claims: src/providers/GitHubProvider.ts: an active FCR-main governance request must first apply and read back a separate strict required-status ruleset with zero bypass actors, exact requested checks, strict current-base policy, active enforcement, and no unexpected rule types before changing the review membrane.

src/providers/GitHubProvider.ts: the FCR review membrane must retain pull-request approval freshness, last-push approval, review-thread resolution, force-push/deletion protection, exactly one numeric trusted GitHub App bypass in pull_request mode, and no bypassable required-status rule.

src/providers/GitHubProvider.ts: canonical FCR integration must bind the provider-backed reviewed PR number to freshly resolved exact base and head SHAs, may merge only through the pull-request endpoint, and must propagate provider rejection without falling back to generic direct protected-branch integration.

src/providers/RepositoryProvider.ts: ruleset bypass actors must remain explicit machine identities whose effective bypass scope is chosen and verified by the provider implementation; callers cannot grant themselves broader bypass authority through the provider-neutral contract.

.github/workflows/quality-gate.yml: every pull-request Quality Gate job must checkout and verify the exact github.event.pull_request.head.sha before tests or builds, and a synthetic PR merge ref cannot satisfy exact-head candidate proof.
src/buildEvents/buildEvent.ts: coverage events must retain bounded aggregate-only shape validation and cannot carry raw request evidence.

src/buildEvents/currentTruth.ts: webhook main facts must remain last-observed provenance, current coverage must use a fresh read-through GitHub revalidation and passed verified lease, and legacy external operational assertions cannot render as current.

src/buildEvents/currentMainRevalidation.ts: current-main identity must be read from the enrolled GitHub provider at display time, bind the enrolled repository and `main` branch, and reject a non-exact SHA.

src/buildEvents/releaseCoverageWitness.ts: a passed coverage claim must require a server-owned exact-target Cloudflare witness, deployment-to-window ordering, an independently written aggregate digest, and the canonical App-aware repository credential path.

src/http/routes/buildEventReceipts.ts: the release-observer credential must be project-bound Cloudflare analytics coverage only, reject control-plane fields and non-passed receipts, and require the matching independent witness.
scripts/verify-documentation-truth.mjs: truth-sensitive changes must reject punctuation-only or hidden-comment documentation edits and require a meaningful path-bound invariant receipt.

src/providers/RepositoryProviderFactory.ts: repository reads that need production identity proof must reject partial GitHub App credentials and otherwise prefer a repository-scoped installation credential over an explicit local fallback.
src/services/buildEventStore.ts: the bounded feed must retain the newest GitHub-observed main source as historical provenance without treating webhook arrival order as current-main proof.
src/http/routes/buildEvents.ts: the current-truth route must bind projection evaluation to the enrolled project repository and fail closed when that repository identity is unavailable.

src/governance/portfolioDecisionContext.ts: evidence-dependent consequential portfolio execution must bind founder authorization to the exact normalized decision-context Truth Lease and re-evaluate fresh dependency observations at the use boundary; stale, changed, missing, invalid, or unbound truth must reconfirm instead of execute.

src/governance/productionTruthLease.ts: a production-truth lease may exist only when Cloudflare Worker/Pages identity, Playwright tested/runtime identity, independent review, Supabase production state, and repository main identity are bound to one exact candidate; any changed, stale, missing, or mismatched dependency must fail closed at use time.
